questions.text: What exactly does "Place order" receive and who calls it: the user's browser, the Cart service, or the Order service? And what does it create first?
What does "Reserve stock" do in Inventory: lock specific items, decrement a count, or something else? What does the caller get back, and what happens if there is not enough stock?
When "Take payment" runs, is the call to the payment provider synchronous? What does the provider return right away, and which service owns the payment record?
What does the "Payment webhook" contain, who receives it (Payment or Order service), and how does it tell Order to confirm?
If the provider reports the payment failed or the customer abandons it, what happens to the reservation and the order status?
What does "dedupe" mean here: what key identifies a duplicate webhook, and where is it stored?
questions.about: Webhooks can be late or duplicated, so dedupe

questions.text: In the diagram, "Confirm order" leads to both "Clear cart" and "Refund". Is Refund a normal step after every confirmation, or only in the late-payment case? What decides?
What is the full list of order statuses, and which service updates each one?

answers.text: The browser calls Order's start-checkout endpoint with the cart id. Order asks Cart for the lines and prices, then saves the order as pending with that copy before it calls Inventory. Order owns the order record and its status, and the snapshot must be taken at this moment.

Inventory does not lock items or decrement a count while waiting. It saves one hold per order that lists all lines and expires 10 minutes later. Free stock is on-hand minus unexpired holds, so an expired hold frees stock with no cleanup job. The caller gets 'reserved' or the list of short items. On a short result nothing is saved, which gives all-or-nothing.

The brief does not say what the provider returns right away. The plan does not depend on it: Payment saves the charge as pending whatever the reply, and only the webhook decides the outcome. Payment owns the payment record because the brief says only Payment talks to the provider.

Payment receives the webhook, because only Payment talks to the provider. It then publishes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined, and Order confirms on that event. The webhook's exact contents are not in the brief. The plan needs it to carry the order id and a unique event id, which is listed in Open questions.

Declined: Payment stores declined and publishes PaymentDeclined. Order sets the order to cancelled (payment declined) and asks Inventory to release the hold. The brief does not cover a checkout that is abandoned with no webhook ever arriving. The file lists this in Open questions and sets no rule for it.

The key is the provider's event id, which repeats when the same webhook is resent. Payment stores each processed id in a table in its own database, written in the same transaction as the charge status change, so a repeat finds it and does nothing. This assumes the provider gives each event a unique id, which must be checked in its docs.

Only in the late case. The brief says a payment that succeeds after the stock has gone is refunded automatically. Refund is not a normal step after confirmation. The draft's arrow from Confirm to Refund was wrong and is removed.

Order statuses are pending, confirmed and cancelled. Cancelled carries a reason: short stock, payment declined or out of stock. Only Order sets them. Refund progress is kept by Payment, not Order, because Payment owns refunds.

questions.text: After Order saves the pending order, what makes it go on to call Inventory? If Order crashes between those two moments, what picks the order up again, or does it stay pending?
questions.about: Step 1 Place order / Step 2 Reserve stock

questions.text: The provider's immediate reply is not used. If the provider rejects the charge at once, or never responds, what does Order or the customer see before any webhook arrives?
Order retries the charge with the same order id. How many times, and for how long? What happens to the hold and the order if every retry fails?
After Payment publishes PaymentSucceeded, how does Order hear it and then call Inventory? Is that the same broker event described in Terms?
questions.about: Step 4 Payment webhook -> Step 6 Claim stock

questions.text: When the hold has expired and Inventory reserves again, does that make a new hold and claim it in the same call? What exactly does 'claimed' mean in that case?
How does Payment learn that it must refund: does Order call it, or does an event trigger it? What does the customer see while the refund is still pending?
Order releases the hold on PaymentDeclined. If the hold has already expired, or was never claimed, what does the release do? Does the order's cancellation depend on the release succeeding?

answers.text: Order calls Inventory right after it saves the pending order, in the same request. Nothing picks the order up if Order crashes between the two. The brief has no recovery job, so the order stays pending with no hold and no charge. The customer sees no confirmation and can press Place order again. Cleaning up stranded pending orders is listed in Open questions.

The plan ignores the provider's immediate reply, so before any webhook the order stays pending and the customer sees 'payment processing'. Only the webhook sets the outcome, as the brief requires. Whether the provider sends a webhook after an immediate rejection is not known, so it is listed in Open questions.

The brief gives no retry count or spacing, so the file does not set one. It is listed in Open questions. Decided: every retry reuses the order id, so the provider cannot charge twice. If every retry fails, the order stays pending and the hold lapses. If the provider did take the charge, its webhook still arrives and step 4 handles it.

Order subscribes to the PaymentSucceeded event on the shared broker. This is the same kind of event as the Event term. Order then calls Inventory over HTTP to claim the stock. The file now says this in step 6.

Yes. When the hold has expired, Inventory runs the all-or-nothing reserve and, if every line fits, saves a new hold and marks it claimed in one transaction. 'Claimed' means the stock is sold: on-hand drops by the quantity, and the claimed hold no longer counts as a hold. Both terms are now defined in Terms and step 6.

Order calls Payment over HTTP to request the refund, the same way it requests the charge. Payment first saves a refund row as pending, so the refund survives a crash. Then it calls the provider with the order id as key and retries until accepted. While it is pending, the order shows cancelled (out of stock), and the email says the refund is on its way.

Release is a delete of the hold. If the hold has expired or was never saved, there is nothing to delete, so the release does nothing. Cancellation does not depend on the release: Order cancels on PaymentDeclined, then retries the release. A missed release still frees the stock when the hold expires.

questions.text: When Order receives PaymentSucceeded, what happens if Order crashes or its claim call to Inventory keeps failing? Does the broker redeliver the event, and how long does Order keep retrying?
If every claim retry fails, what is the order's status, and has the customer already been charged? What does the customer see?
questions.about: Step 6 Claim stock: If it fails

questions.text: Order sets the order to confirmed and then publishes OrderConfirmed. If Order saves the status but the publish fails, or it crashes between the two, what happens? Does the cart ever get cleared?
How does Payment know which order and which charge a webhook belongs to, and how does the provider reach Payment? Is the order id in the webhook?
After Order asks Payment to refund, what does Order get back, and does Order wait for the provider to accept? Who raises the pending-refund alert, and who acts on it?

answers.text: The brief does not name the broker or its redelivery rules, so it is not known whether an unacknowledged PaymentSucceeded is redelivered. The file now says Order acknowledges the event only after it has a claim result, so a crash before that leaves the event unacknowledged. How long Order keeps retrying is not in the brief and is listed in Open questions. No retry count is invented.

Yes, the customer has been charged: the webhook reported success, so the money is taken. The order stays pending and the customer sees 'payment processing'. The brief says we never keep money for an order we cannot fulfil but gives no rule for a claim that never gets an answer. The plan does not decide this; it is listed in Open questions.

If Order saves confirmed and the publish fails, the file now says Order retries the publish until it succeeds, as Payment does in step 4. If Order crashes between saving and publishing, OrderConfirmed is never sent, the cart is not cleared, and the order stays confirmed. The plan has no rule for this case. Fixing it needs an outbox, which the brief does not ask for, so it is listed in Open questions.

The brief does not say what the webhook contains, so it is not known whether it carries the order id. The file now says Payment finds the charge by the order id in the webhook and flags that the id may be missing, which is listed in Open questions. How the provider reaches Payment is decided: Payment hosts the webhook endpoint, because only Payment talks to the provider.

Order gets back an answer as soon as Payment has saved the refund row as pending. Order does not wait for the provider to accept the refund; Payment calls the provider afterwards and retries until it is accepted. The file now says this in step 7. Who receives the pending-refund alert and who acts on it is not in the brief, so it is unknown and listed in Open questions.

questions.text: After the customer sees "payment processing", how does the browser find out the final result (confirmed or cancelled)? Does it poll Order, or is it pushed something?
questions.about: Step 3 Take payment / Step 7 Confirm or refund

questions.text: Is the charge request to Payment made inside the same browser request as Place order and Reserve stock, or does Order do it separately? When does the browser get its first reply?
questions.about: Step 1 Place order / Step 3 Take payment

questions.text: When Payment publishes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined, how does Order match the event to an order, and what does Order do if that order is already cancelled or confirmed?
questions.about: Step 4 Payment webhook / Step 6 Claim stock

answers.text: The browser polls Order. Order already stores the status (pending, confirmed or cancelled), so the browser asks Order for the status until it is no longer pending. Push (a websocket or server-sent events) is not in the brief and would add a mechanism. The polling interval is a detail and is left out of the file. Added to step 3.

Yes. Steps 1 to 3 run in one browser request. Order saves the pending order, asks Inventory for the hold, and only if the hold succeeds asks Payment to charge. The browser's first reply is either the short items (no charge made) or 'payment processing' (once the charge is saved as pending). This gives the first reply one clear meaning without a second call. Charge retry timing is still an open question (step 3). If every charge retry fails, the browser shows an error and the customer can press Place order again.

Order matches the event by the order id, which Payment puts in PaymentSucceeded and PaymentDeclined. This is Payment's own event field, not a webhook field, so it does not depend on the open question about webhook contents. If the order is already confirmed, Order does nothing and acknowledges the event (a repeat). If it is pending, Order claims the stock. If it is already cancelled, Order does not claim and refunds, because we never keep money for a cancelled order. This last case should not happen in this plan, since a cancelled order is never charged. Added to step 6.

teachbacks.text:
1. Customer presses Place order. The browser calls Order's start-checkout endpoint with the cart id. This starts one browser request that also covers steps 2 and 3.
2. Order asks Cart for the cart's lines and prices. It saves an order row as "pending" in Order's own database, with a copy of those lines and prices. Each press creates a new order id. If the Cart call or the save fails, the customer sees an error and the cart is unchanged. If Order crashes after the save, nothing is reserved or charged and the order stays pending. The customer can press Place order again.
3. Order calls Inventory with the order id and the lines. In one transaction, Inventory checks that every line fits in free stock (on-hand minus unexpired holds). If all fit, it saves one hold row for the order, expiring in 10 minutes. If any line is short, it saves nothing and returns the short items. Order then cancels with reason "short stock", the browser shows the short items, no payment is requested and the cart is untouched. If the call itself fails, Order retries with the same order id, which is safe because Inventory keeps one hold per order id.
4. After the hold succeeds, Order asks Payment to charge the order total. Payment saves a charge row as pending in its own database, then sends the charge to the provider with the order id as idempotency key. The provider's immediate reply is ignored. Once the charge is saved as pending, Place order replies to the browser with "payment processing". The browser then polls Order's status until it is no longer pending, and shows confirmed, or cancelled with its reason. If the charge call fails, Order retries with the same order id so the provider cannot charge twice. If every retry fails, the browser shows an error, the order stays pending, the hold lapses after 10 minutes and no charge is known. The customer can press Place order again.
5. Later, from seconds to 30 minutes, the provider sends a webhook to Payment's endpoint. It may arrive more than once. Payment checks whether the event id is already stored. If it is, Payment does nothing. Otherwise, in one transaction, it stores the event id, finds the charge by order id and sets it to succeeded or declined. Then it publishes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined on the broker. If the transaction fails, nothing is stored and the provider's resend is treated as new. If publishing fails, Payment retries until it is published.
6. Declined path. Order receives PaymentDeclined. It sets the order to cancelled with reason "payment declined" and asks Inventory to release the hold. The cancel does not wait for the release. Inventory deletes the hold row. If the release fails, Order retries it, and a missed release still frees the stock when the hold expires. Releasing an expired or missing hold does nothing. The cart is unchanged. The browser's polling then shows the cancelled order.
7. Succeeded path. Order receives PaymentSucceeded, which carries the order id, and looks up the order. If the order is already confirmed, it does nothing and acknowledges the event. If the order is already cancelled, which is not expected, it skips the claim and refunds (step 9). If the order is pending, Order calls Inventory over HTTP to claim the stock.
8. Claim. If the hold is still active, Inventory marks it claimed. If the hold is expired or missing, Inventory reruns the all-or-nothing reserve for the same lines. If everything fits, it saves a new hold marked claimed, replacing any old expired hold for that order id. If any line does not fit, it saves nothing. The result is claimed or not claimed. A repeat claim on an already-claimed order returns claimed. Order retries the claim with the order id on failure. It acknowledges PaymentSucceeded only after it has a result.
9. If the claim result is "claimed", Order sets the order to confirmed and publishes OrderConfirmed. It retries the publish until it succeeds. The browser's poll now shows confirmed. If the result is "not claimed", Order sets the order to cancelled with reason "out of stock" and emails the customer. It then asks Payment to refund the full amount. Payment saves a refund row as pending and replies to Order. It then calls the provider with the order id as key and retries until the provider accepts, then marks the row refunded. Order does not wait for the provider. If Payment cannot save the row, Order retries with the same order id. A pending refund raises an alert. Until the refund is accepted, the customer sees "cancelled, out of stock" and the email says the refund is on its way.
10. Cart clears. Cart subscribes to OrderConfirmed and empties the cart in its own database. If this fails, the broker redelivers the event, and emptying an empty cart does nothing. The cart changes only on this event, so every earlier failure leaves it as it was.
gaps: How Order learns about PaymentDeclined is not stated for the broker side. Step 6 says Order starts on the event, but the document does not say Order subscribes or acknowledges it the way it does for PaymentSucceeded.
The document does not say what the webhook contains. It does not say whether it carries the order id and a unique event id, so I cannot say how Payment finds the charge or dedupes events.
How many times Order retries the charge, the claim, the release and the refund request, and the spacing between retries, is not given. How long Order keeps trying is also not given.
Whether the broker redelivers unacknowledged events is unknown. This matters if Order crashes before acknowledging PaymentSucceeded.
What happens when the claim never returns a result is not stated. The customer is charged, the order stays pending, and no refund path exists.
Who or what cancels pending orders that never get a webhook or were stranded by a crash is not stated. This includes the case where the provider rejects the charge instantly and sends no webhook.
What happens if Order crashes after saving confirmed but before publishing OrderConfirmed is not covered. The cart is never cleared and no recovery exists.
Who receives the pending-refund alert, who acts on it, and how many refund retries come before it is not stated.

The document does not say how the order's final cancel or confirm status gets to the customer apart from the browser polling. It also does not say what the customer sees if they poll after an out-of-stock refund when the stock was re-reserved by a late payment, because the plan marks this as unconfirmed behaviour.

The document does not say how the 'charge' call returns to Order, or when Order decides the charge request succeeded, other than Payment saving the row as pending and Place order replying 'payment processing'.
